## 1. Concept Overview

Under the (-,+,+,+) convention the Lagrangian is **L = X − V(φ)** with X = −(½)g^μν∂_μφ∂_νφ, giving w = (X − V)/(X + V) ∈ [−1, 1]. Its non-canonical generalization is k-essence (Armendariz-Picon, Mukhanov & Steinhardt 2000; Copeland, Sami & Tsujikawa 2006, DOI: 10.1142/S021827180600942X), with general P(X, φ) and sound speed c_s² = P_,X/(P_,X + 2XP_,XX).

**Key empirical fact (stated explicitly, per researcher needs):** to date there is **no empirical discrimination between quintessence and k-essence** from background observables alone — both can produce identical w(a) histories; only the perturbation sound speed c_s² (or non-Gaussian signatures) differs in principle, and current data (DESI, Planck, SNe) do not yet resolve it.

## 1. Concept Overview

K-essence (Armendariz-Picon, Mukhanov & Steinhardt 2001, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevD.63.103510; 1841 citations) generalizes canonical quintessence (Peebles & Ratra 2003, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.75.559) by replacing the canonical kinetic term with a general function of the kinetic invariant:

$$\mathcal{L}_{k\text{-ess}} = K(X) - V(\phi) \quad\text{or generally}\quad \mathcal{L} = P(X,\phi),$$

with $X \equiv -\tfrac12 g^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial_\nu\phi > 0$ on homogeneous backgrounds. Its modern, most general ghost-free descendant is the KGB (Kinetic Gravity Braiding) class (Deffayet, Pujolàs, Sawicki & Vikman 2010, JCAP 10, 026, DOI: 10.1088/1475-7516/2010/10/026, arXiv:1008.0048, 705 citations), whose Lagrangian contains second-derivative interactions without extra degrees of freedom (Kobayashi 2019 Horndeski review, DOI: 10.1088/1361-6633/ab2429, 614 citations).

**Explicit empirical statement (mandated):** to date there is **no empirical discrimination between quintessence and k-essence**. Background observables ($H(z)$, SNe luminosity distances, BAO) depend only on $w(a)$, which both classes can reproduce identically. Only perturbation-level probes — the scalar sound speed $c_s^2$, dark-energy clustering, or non-Gaussianity — differ in principle, and current data (DESI, Planck, SNe, Euclid/Y1) do not resolve them.
